newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee dips vs forward dollar as call spurts.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee dips vs forward dollar as call spurts.

text.p: The rupee eased mildly against the spot and forward dollar on Wednesday noon, dealers said.
Dollar bids by the State Bank of India and other banks pushed the rupee to 35.77/78 from 35.765/775, dealers said.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told Reuters Financial Television in Washington that the central bank was leaving the exchange rate to forces of demand and supply for the time being.
He said large capital inflows had led to an appreciation of the nominal exchange rate of the rupee.
The rupee eased slightly against the forward dollar on the back of a spurt in overnight call money rates, dealers said.
November dollars were quoted at 0.88/0.93 rupees on Wednesday afternoon, up from the earlier level of 0.87/0.89 rupees, dealers said.
Call rates spurted to 3.5-4.25 percent on Wednesday from 0.50-0.75 percent opening on expectations a state government loan issue later on Wednesday will be heavily oversubscribed, dealers said.
But some analysts said Wednesday's mild rise in forward premiums was an aberration.
"The tailspin (in premiums) continues," said Yeshwant Rao, deputy general manager (forex) at Arvind Mills, referring to the downtrend in forward premiums in recent weeks.
"I think there is good chance (for six month annualised premium) to hit 3.5 percent." The six month premium closed Tuesday at 4.36 percent.
